name: PT Bakrie & Brothers Tbk

frontmatter.title: Bakrie & Brothers: a toll road and a book-valued EV stake inside a family holding company
frontmatter.summary: BNBR is the Bakrie family's listed vehicle: a toll road to 2061, a large but uncovered listed EV sibling now carried at book, and steel and digital businesses worth less than book. Earnings are one-off, the first half of 2026 was a loss, the family funds itself by issuing shares, and the shares trade well above the marked value of the parts. We keep HOLD: the fundamental value sits below the price, and only the konglo lens's most-likely-premium step bridges the gap.
thesis: Only two parts carry a mark that is not a pure residual - the Cimanggis-Cibitung toll road at its audited acquisition fair value and the listed VKTR stake, now at book because VKTR is an uncovered konglo sibling - and once the residual, the wide holdco discount and the post-rights bridge are applied, the sum of the parts is below the traded price.

Almost all of the value that reaches the parent is one asset's cash flow, and the debt that finances it sits inside the part: the project syndicated loan is a multiple of the toll road's net asset value, and the first half of 2026 ran at a loss because the floating-rate interest landed before the revenue ramped.

Reported profit is not a guide: FY2025 earnings were carried by a one-off bargain-purchase gain, FY2024 by gains on loan settlements and asset sales, and the accumulated deficit was erased by a quasi-reorganization, so the earnings history cannot anchor a multiple.
The P/E leg is inapplicable and the P/BV cross-check only works once book equity is restated for the July rights issue; the sum of the parts carries most of the weight.

Governance is the discount's DNA: control sits behind offshore vehicles, the float is a minority, related-party balances are large and equity issuance is the family's funding instrument, so the discount is set wide and no dated narrowing catalyst exists.

The bull is a genuine motorway that would be worth more on a house DCF than at its acquisition mark, plus the EV order book and a tariff increase; none of those inputs is sourced well enough to capitalise, so they sit in the sensitivity and the bull narrative rather than in the base.

catalysts.event: Third-quarter report, the first balance sheet to carry the July rights issue and the debt repayment
The 2026 toll tariff adjustment on the Cimanggis-Cibitung section
Full-year 2026 results, with the first clean read on whether the group covers its interest
Annual shareholders' meeting and any decision on the accumulated-loss position and a dividend
Regime - MSCI's decision on moving Indonesia to Standalone status, which would affect concentrated-ownership names

blocks.text: **What changed.** This revision answers the red team's round. Three things move the numbers and one corrects a fact. First, the sum of the parts now carries the listed VKTR stake at **book**, not at market: VKTR is a konglo:true member of the Bakrie group, it is not covered, and the group-consistency rule forbids marking an uncovered konglo sibling at its listed premium. The Director's ruling of 28 October 2026 requires a sourced non-market basis, so VKTR is carried at BNBR's share of VKTR net assets from the audited balance sheet, with the market premium excluded. Second, the P/BV cross-check is now struck on post-rights book equity, so it no longer divides pre-rights equity by post-rights shares. Third, the scenarios are stated for what they are - a discount-and-earnings sensitivity, not a re-mark of the parts. The governance section no longer claims an HSC listing the registry denies.

We rate PT Bakrie & Brothers at **HOLD** with a target of **Rp52** against a last price of **Rp51**, a total return of **2.4%** [S0]. The twelve-month fundamental value is **Rp34**, below today's price; the target sits above it only because the konglo lens keeps part of the premium the market pays [S0]. The call is deliberately narrow: it is not a view that Indonesian toll demand is weak - it is not - but that the listed parent, valued on its parts, is worth less than the shares cost, and the regime premium the lens carries is the most likely twelve-month price only because float and flows, not fundamentals, set the marginal price of a name like this.

Three things set the file. First, the group rises or falls on one operating asset and one large listed stake. The Cimanggis-Cibitung toll road, consolidated on 28 November 2025, carries a concession to 2061 and was recognised in the group's own acquisition accounting at identifiable assets of **15,896** less identifiable liabilities of **11,579** [S18, S12]; alongside it sits the VKTR stake, an uncovered konglo sibling now carried at book [S12]. Everything else the company owns, once those two parts are carved out, leaves the parent with negative book value, because the rest of the group's equity is largely the non-controlling interest's [S12]. Second, the toll road's debt is the group's debt: the project syndicated loan alone is **9,715** [S12], and the company attributes the first-half 2026 loss to the floating-rate interest on that toll road arriving before its revenue ramped [S5]. Third, the profit history is not a history of profits: FY2025's result is dominated by a **320** one-off bargain-purchase gain and a **422** remeasurement gain, and the accumulated deficit was extinguished by a quasi-reorganization in 2024 [S11, S12].

A holding company trades at a discount to the value of the assets it controls, and that discount is
not an anomaly to be arbitraged: it is the normal state of affairs, and it persists because the
minority shareholder cannot force the value out. It narrows when something happens that deliberately
moves cash or ownership towards the parent's shareholders, so the reason to expect a narrower
discount is that a dated event will change it, not that the discount exists.

What moves the value? The tariff schedule on the motorway and the traffic that runs over it; the interest rate the group pays on the loan that financed it, which is floating; and whether the manufacturing, electric-vehicle and digital businesses ever earn their cost of capital, which at present they do not [S3, S5]. Against that, the price already assumes that all three go right.

BNBR is the listed vehicle through which the Bakrie family holds a set of industrial and infrastructure businesses. The company describes itself as a multi-sector investment holding company and reports three segments: infrastructure and manufacturing, fabrication and construction services, and trading, services and investment [S12]. Its largest businesses by revenue in FY2025 were the steel structure, pipe and construction group PT Bakrie Metal Industries, which contributed **2,200**, and the electric-vehicle group PT VKTR Teknologi Mobilitas Tbk, which contributed **1,080**; the infrastructure business PT Bakrie Indo Infrastructure contributed **464**, and the digital-infrastructure arm PT Multi Kontrol Nusantara, whose revenue rose by about a sixth to **359**, runs a fibre and homepass network under government connectivity programmes [S2]. The footprint is domestic: the toll road is in Greater Jakarta, the steel and pipe businesses serve oil, gas and infrastructure customers from Bekasi, and the electric-vehicle assembly plant is in Magelang [S15].

The business that matters is the toll road. PT Cimanggis Cibitung Tollways operates the section between the Cimanggis and Cibitung junctions as part of the outer ring network, with a concession running to 10 August 2061; it has been fully operational since 2024, and traffic in the eight months to August 2026 averaged **43,911** vehicles a day, above the company's own budget, on revenue of **2,500** per day [S15, S18]. The group took its ownership of the concession from a tenth to full control on 28 November 2025, buying out PT Sarana Multi Infrastruktur and PT Waskita Toll Road and taking over the shareholder loans they had extended [S12, S18]. We make no claim of a concession extension: the archive states the term and nothing beyond it, and the bull relies on the traffic and tariff upside, not on a life extension.

The rest of the group is smaller and thinner than its revenue suggests. The steel, pipe and construction businesses sell into oil and gas and into public infrastructure; Bakrie Autoparts, now held through the electric-vehicle arm, supplies automotive components to original-equipment manufacturers; VKTR assembles electric buses for TransJakarta and states that it is the only supplier meeting the domestic-content requirement for the twelve-metre fleet [S2, S15]. There are also early-stage businesses in rooftop solar and electric-vehicle charging through Bakrie Power and Helio Synar Energi, and a three-dimensional construction printing venture with a Danish partner [S2].

Control is family-based and indirect. The company's stated controlling shareholders are Aburizal, Nirwan Dermawan and Indra Usmansjah Bakrie, holding through a chain of vehicles, and the largest single registered shareholder in the corporate structure is an offshore company holding **26.0%**; the free float is **30.0%** [S11]. BNBR is therefore a holding company in the strict sense: what its shareholders own is a claim on subsidiaries that are themselves controlled by the family, and what those shares are worth is the ability to extract value from those subsidiaries.

The sectors BNBR operates in are not one industry, and the house treats it as a conglomerate rather than as a company in any of them. The macro backdrop is a balance-of-payments pressure regime under which the division tilts towards export-supply-discipline names and away from Indonesian rate-sensitive domestic demand, which is the wrong side of the tilt for a group whose largest business is a domestic toll concession and whose balance sheet is floating-rate [S0].

The toll road is where the industry question actually lives, and it is a regulated-concession business rather than a competitive one. The concession sets the tariff and the term; the value comes from traffic growth over a period long enough that the early years of debt service do not determine the outcome. Cimanggis-Cibitung is the final section of the outer ring network, connecting the Soekarno-Hatta airport corridor to the Tanjung Priok port hinterland, and it competes for traffic with the Jakarta inner ring and with the Jakarta-Cikampek corridor [S15]. It is a toll road in a densely populated catchment, and its own traffic is running above both its internal budget and the company's comparison set of similar roads [S15]. That is a genuinely good asset.

The rest of the group competes in industries where it is a challenger rather than a leader. The steel-pipe and fabrication business sells into oil and gas and into infrastructure spending; the automotive-components business sells to vehicle manufacturers and is exposed to domestic purchasing power; the electric-vehicle business depends on a public-policy-driven procurement stream and on domestic-content rules [S2, S15]. None of them has the pricing power of a concession, and their combined contribution to the group's profit is not visible as a separate, positive parent-attributable number [S12].

Regulation and policy are therefore the dominant external influences. Toll tariffs are set by the regulator, so the timing of an adjustment matters more than any commercial decision the operator makes; the electric-vehicle business depends on government procurement and on local-content rules; and the group's infrastructure and connectivity contracts are awarded by the state [S15]. The macroeconomic influences are the rupiah, which determines the cost of the dollar-denominated portion of the group's borrowing, and the floating-rate environment, which the company singled out when it explained why its first half of 2026 was a loss [S5].

On a five-forces reading, the toll road has a negligible threat of new entry and no substitute within its corridor, which is why it is the only part of the group worth close to its carrying value; the manufacturing and components businesses face import competition, fragmented customers and modest switching costs, and their returns reflect that. The moat, in one sentence, is the concession document, and it belongs to one subsidiary: the group cannot replicate it, its competitors cannot attack it, and every other business in the group has to earn its keep against one. That is the whole of the competitive advantage. [S12, S15]

FY2025 revenue was **3,743** on a consolidated basis, slightly lower than the prior year, and the audited statements show why the reported profit should not be read as earnings power. Gross profit of **744** left an operating profit of only **117** after operating expenses of **628**, so essentially the entire profit for the year came below the operating line [S12]. That below-the-line result includes a gain of **320** on the bargain purchase of the toll road, foreign-exchange and asset-sale gains, and the reversal of a receivable provision, net of interest and financial charges [S12].

Depreciation and amortisation is one line where the data pack is wrong. The audited notes show **171** of depreciation and amortisation for FY2025 allocated between the cost of revenue and general and administrative expenses, where the pack carries only the latter; restating it, and the operating lines with it, takes FY2025 EBITDA to **288** [S12, F6]. The operating lines are restated the same way: the pack's operating expenses and operating profit came from a different allocation than the filing's Total Beban Usaha and LABA USAHA, which leave FY2025 operating expenses of **628** and an operating profit of **117** [S12, F52, F54]. The pack's share count is wrong as well: the audited statements show **173,417**m shares in issue at the end of FY2025 rather than the larger number the pack carries, and every per-share figure here is struck on the post-rights total that filed count grosses up to under the July 2026 rights issue, not on the pack's number [S12, F8].

Our forecast carries the toll road's first full year. FY2026E revenue of **5,165** is a step of about two-fifths on FY2025, because the toll road was consolidated only from the end of November and the first half of 2026 alone produced **2,590** of revenue, with the company attributing the growth to the toll road's consolidation and to electric-vehicle sales [S3, S5]. We hold the gross margin at the reported first-half ratio of about a quarter of revenue rather than FY2025's lower figure, and operating expenses at the reported first-half ratio, a little over a seventh of sales, because the FY2025 ratios were struck on a revenue base less than half the size and a haircut to the reported ratios would be an unexplained caution [S0, S3]. Those ratios are derived from the pack's first-half quarterly gross-profit and operating-expense lines, which reconcile to the revenue the company reports; it is the pack's D&A, EBIT and share-count fields that the filing contradicts, not these top-line lines [S0, S3]. EBITDA on that basis is **821**, a margin of **15.9%** against FY2025's **7.7%** [S0, S12].

The forecast then shows the file's central problem. Interest expense is struck on opening debt at about **6.5%** a year, the first-half 2026 rate annualised, and that interest bill is larger than the operating profit the group generates in every forecast year, so the model runs small losses throughout: net profit to the parent is **-431** and stays negative [S0, S5]. Net debt is **16,207**, or **19.7**x EBITDA, against operating profit of **563** and interest of **1,089** - cover below one times [S0]. The company's own explanation of the first-half loss is the same arithmetic: the floating-rate interest on the toll road landed before its revenue ramped [S5]. Working capital is a further drag, because the group carries operating working capital at a little under two-fifths of revenue, largely related-party, so growth consumes cash rather than releasing it [S0].

Two limitations of this projection must be stated. It gives no credit for the July 2026 rights issue: the engine's cash-flow template has no line for an equity issuance, so the capital action that raised the equity and repaid group debt cannot be shown as one movement, and the repayment is carried in the valuation bridge instead [S5, S16, S19]. Interest expense is therefore struck on a debt balance about **4,362** too high for the years after the repayment, and the losses we show are wider than the post-issue reality; nothing in the rating depends on it, because the call is set by the sum of the parts and the cross-checks rather than by the projected profit and loss account. Separately, the forecast funds the group's cash deficit and rolling maturities with new borrowing at the last actual's scale rather than with a dated facility, which is a stated financing assumption rather than a sourced plan [S0, S12].

Capital allocation has run one way for years: towards the family's other vehicles, and towards issuing shares. The equity has been enlarged by a series of capital increases, and the accumulated deficit stood at a level that required a quasi-reorganization in 2024, which eliminated **19,530** of accumulated losses and reset the comparability of the equity and earnings history [S11, S12]. Dividends have not been paid in the period covered by the price history, and the policy makes any future payout conditional on financial condition and a shareholders' resolution [S6].

The house method for a conglomerate values it on its parts, because a consolidated multiple applied to a group like this one measures the largest subsidiary and calls it the whole. We build the sum from three things, each labelled with its method: the toll road at the audited acquisition fair value, the listed VKTR stake at **book** because VKTR is an uncovered konglo sibling, and everything else at book.

The toll road is carried at the group's share of the price its own November 2025 business combination put on it: identifiable assets acquired of **15,896** less identifiable liabilities assumed of **11,579** less the non-controlling-interest portion leaves net assets acquired of **4,101** [S12, F12, F13, F44]. That is the one third-party mark on a group asset, and it is the company's own. It is not a house DCF, and we say why: the record carries traffic, daily revenue, standalone revenue and EBITDA and the concession term, but no tariff schedule and no traffic forecast, so a DCF would have to invent both the tariff path and the growth rate. An invented path is not a sourced mark, so the acquisition fair value is the base and the CCT upside sits in the sensitivity and the bull narrative below.

VKTR, the listed electric-vehicle subsidiary, is a konglo:true member of the Bakrie group and is not covered. The group-consistency rule forbids marking an uncovered konglo sibling at market, because its listed premium would enter the parent's fundamental value; the Director's ruling of 28 October 2026 requires a sourced non-market basis because the stage machine cannot return BNBR to draft. VKTR is therefore carried at the book value of BNBR's stake from the latest audited balance sheet: VKTR's non-controlling interest of **812** at a minority of about three-quarters implies VKTR net assets, of which BNBR's **24.4%** share is **262** [S12, F45, F49, F58]. The market mark it replaces - the holding at the IDX theoretical ex-rights price of **675** a share against the cum price of **835** [S23, F38, F39] - is excluded, and with it the sibling's listed premium. The mark switches to house value once VKTR is covered and publishes; until then book is the honest basis.

The below-market sensitivity on VKTR is the range between book and the price a standby buyer actually paid. At VKTR's own October 2026 rights-issue exercise price the stake would be worth **2,135** rather than **262** at book [S23, F57, F58]. Both are far below the market mark; the floor would lift the SOTP materially but still leave the fundamental value below today's price. We do not use the floor in the base because it is a subscription price, not a fundamental value, and the Director's ruling fixes book as the base with the floor as the sensitivity.

Everything else - the steel and pipe group, the components business, the digital-infrastructure and power businesses - is carried at book, and stated as such. That residual line is negative: consolidated parent equity of **3,853** less the toll road's group share and less the VKTR book value leaves less than nothing, because the CCT acquisition recognised net assets above the consideration paid, the retained-earnings base is thin after the quasi-reorganization, and the group debt and negative-equity subsidiaries outside the two marked parts sit here - including Bakrie Metal Industries, whose own non-controlling interest is negative at **-1** [S12]. It is book, not a house-card valuation: we hold it there rather than at zero because the businesses trade and generate revenue, and the bull case is that they are worth more than book. No segment EBITDA for BMI is archived, so a house mark cannot be sourced yet; the zero-floor and a modest positive mark are shown in the sensitivity discussion, not capitalised.

Two post-balance-sheet items go into the bridge. The July 2026 rights issue raised **4,760** from **89,920** new shares at **53** each; of the proceeds **4,362** repaid in full the facility the group's subsidiary owed to Hartman International and Bank Nobu, and the balance funded working capital, the BCI construction capital, the CCT rest-area equity and company operations [S16, S19, F42]. The first half of 2026 ran at a loss, which subtracts from them once, because both marked parts are carried at 31 December 2025 book values and the H1 loss is not already inside either mark [S15, F43]. Because the group's debt sits inside each part's net asset value, no further deduction is made for it and the remaining debt is disclosed in the parts. A holding-company discount of **38%** is then applied, at the wide end of the band house sums-of-parts discounts persist in, because this file carries every flag that keeps such discounts wide: control behind offshore vehicles, a minority float, a quasi-reorganization that reset the equity, repeated issuance, and no dividend [S11, S12].

The primary method produces **Rp20** per share [S0]. The cost of capital inside the model is high and is meant to be: with the group's debt-to-equity at **1.65** the levered beta is **2.06**, the cost of equity is **19.6%** and the weighted average cost of capital is **12.0%** [S0]. That is what a holding company with a floating-rate debt load and a single operating asset should be discounted at, and it is not the constraint on the valuation; the marks are.

The cross-check is set on the peer median rather than this company's own five-year average, and the override is stated in the assumptions with its reason. The data pack's own-history multiples are struck on a share count the audited statements contradict and on an equity and earnings series the quasi-reorganization reset, so they are not a benchmark for today's net assets [S11, S12, F8]. On the peer median the P/BV leg produces **Rp63** per share [S0] - now on post-rights book equity, not the pre-rights base the first draft used, so it no longer understates the book claim. It sits far above the primary, and the divergence is the message: book equity is a claim on the whole consolidated group, including assets the SOTP marks conservatively, so it is a loose upper reference, not independent evidence about the parts.

The P/E leg is **removed**, not merely discounted. A P/E is a price for maintainable earnings and there are none here: FY2025 reported parent profit of **494** carries the **320** gain on bargain purchase and the **422** gain on remeasurement of the previously held equity interest in the toll road, both struck on the November 2025 acquisition and neither repeatable [S12, F14, F56]; the parent is loss-making in every forecast year. Strip the one-offs out and the figure turns negative, so the leg is inapplicable rather than merely low, and its weight moved to the parts and the book cross-check.

**Mark sensitivity.** The table above is the configured discount-and-cost-of-capital grid; the mark sensitivity is separate and is stated here because the live methods carry fixed part values. On CCT, a house value above the acquisition mark would raise the SOTP, but no tariff schedule or traffic forecast is archived, so it cannot be sourced and is not capitalised. On VKTR, the floor at **2,135** against book at **262** is the sourced range [F57, F58]. On the residual, a zero floor instead of the negative book number adds back a small amount, and a positive mark for BMI would add more, but no BMI segment accounts are archived. These are the untested levers, and they all point one way - up - which is why the base is the conservative end of the sourced range, not a cautious haircut on it.

What today's price implies is the clearest statement of the gap. The reverse of the primary method cannot be solved at a positive discount: even at a zero holding-company discount the SOTP is **Rp20** per share before the lens, well below the **Rp51** price, so today's price implies a premium to the undiscounted parts, not a discount to them - against the **38%** the governance and history warrant [S0]. A buyer at this price is paying for the option that the toll road is worth far more than its acquisition mark, that the EV business becomes profitable, and that the other assets are worth more than book.

One housekeeping note on the market data: the data pack's own market-capitalisation line is struck on the pack's share base rather than on the post-rights count, so it is carried here only as an unadjusted engine figure and no per-share mark in this report rests on it [S0].

**The konglo lens.** BNBR is a Bakrie-family holding vehicle with a free float of **28.8%** [S0], and in the 2026 regime the marginal price of such a name is set by float and flows rather than by fundamentals. The fundamental value we build above is **Rp34** a share; the market pays **Rp51**, a premium of **1.82x** value, and the lens asks how much of that gap survives the next twelve months. In the base regime scenario it keeps **30%** of the log gap, giving a target of **Rp52**; the bear scenario closes more of it and the bull scenario lets it widen [S0]. The premium is treated as a regime variable, never as an input: our marks are our own and are unchanged, and the lens step is deterministic and visible. The regime flags this name carries are set out in the governance section.
The risks are concentrated and mostly correlated, which is itself the point.

**Interest and refinancing (high likelihood, high impact).** The group's operating profit does not cover its interest expense in any year of our forecast, and the company attributes the first-half 2026 loss to the floating-rate interest on the toll road [S5]. A further rise in the rate the syndicated lenders charge, or a failure to refinance on comparable terms when the current agreement runs, moves the equity directly. The facility's amendments extended its term and reset its rate following the change of control, which tells the reader that the lenders, not the company, set the terms [S12].

**Governance and related-party gravity (high likelihood, medium impact).** The controlling family holds through offshore vehicles and the float is a minority [S11]. The group transacts with affiliates, holds short-term investments in the family's other listed companies, and has repeatedly used equity issuance as its funding instrument, most recently a rights issue struck above book [S12, S16, F27]. Each of those is a channel through which value can reach the family before it reaches the minority.

**Concentration (medium likelihood, high impact).** One asset dominates, one concession, one corridor. The sum of the parts is the toll road and the listed VKTR stake against a negative residual for everything else, so an adverse toll outcome cannot be diversified away inside the group [S12].

**Earnings quality (observed, not prospective).** The FY2025 result is dominated by a one-off gain and the FY2024 result by gains on loan settlements and asset sales; the accumulated deficit was eliminated by a quasi-reorganization; and the share count in the data pack is wrong [S11, S12]. A reader who anchors on the reported multiple is anchoring on a distortion.

**Equity issuance and liquidity (high likelihood, medium impact).** The rights issue relieved the near-term cash problem by moving a large part of the equity into new hands: it was struck at **53** a share, it diluted a holder who did not subscribe by up to **34%**, and the two largest holders transferred their entitlement to a standby buyer rather than fund it themselves [S16, F27, F28, F50]. A family that funds itself from the equity rather than from cash flow dilutes its minority holders a little every cycle, and the enlarged share count is now the base for every per-share figure here [S12, F8]. The same pattern has just run at VKTR, whose own rights issue diluted non-participating holders by up to **25.5%** [S25, F51].

**The scenario spread is a discount-and-earnings sensitivity, stated plainly.** The live methods are the SOTP, whose part values are fixed, and the P/BV cross-check, whose book equity is fixed; neither consumes revenue growth or cost of debt. The bear and bull scenarios are mirrored on the three drivers - holdco discount, revenue growth and cost of debt - but only the discount reaches the SOTP/PBV blend, so the spread between the scenario values is a discount-only sensitivity. We re-weighted the probabilities to bear **35%**, base **45%** and bull **20%** from the flat first draft, because the regime is hostile to concentrated-ownership names - MSCI froze Indonesian index increases, the exchange's HSC list is being taken out of the IHSG, OJK has fined the parties behind other konglo cases, and the IHSG fell sharply in the year to October - so the base case should reflect that, not a symmetric prior [S0]. The bear gives **Rp31**, the base **Rp34** and the bull **Rp37** [S0].

The bull is still real, but it is not in these shocks: the toll road's traffic is above the company's own budget, a tariff increase is scheduled for 2026, and the Burangkeng interchange adds connectivity to the Jakarta-Japek South road [S15, F18, F36]. A house valuation of that motorway rather than its acquisition mark is what the bull would buy, and the mark sensitivity above shows it cannot be sourced yet. The bear is the mirror plus the dilution already struck: the discount stuck wide, the group still loss-making once the equity has been spent, and holders diluted again [S16, F50]. The asymmetry the method card insists on is unchanged: a narrower discount needs a dated catalyst that moves value to the parent's shareholders, and on the evidence - a rights issue already done, no dividend record, and a family that has historically funded itself from equity - we cannot date one.

**The konglo lens and the regime.** Our business scenarios move the fundamental value; a second, independent set of regime scenarios moves the *premium* to that value, because the marginal price is set by float and flows. Today the market pays **1.82x** our fundamental value of **Rp34**, and the lens keeps **30%** of that log gap in the base regime scenario, for a target of **Rp52**; the bear regime scenario gives **Rp40** and the bull **Rp67** [S0]. The dated regime events that could move the closing share are the exchange's minimum free-float step from March 2027, the quarterly HSC reviews, and MSCI's Standalone consultation with a decision due by 30 June 2027; the house konglo registry records BNBR as **not** on the HSC list as of 22 October 2026, so the HSC index exclusions do not apply to it. Group corporate actions - another rights issue or placement, or a change of control - are the other live regime catalysts [S16].

Signposts that would change the view: a tariff adjustment materially above the scheduled one, a visible reduction in the group's debt once the rights-issue repayment is filed, a concrete and dated plan showing the manufacturing and electric-vehicle businesses earning their cost of capital, or any transaction that upstreams cash towards the parent's shareholders rather than away from them.

Ownership and control are the heart of the file. The company's ultimate beneficial owners are the three Bakrie brothers, identified through direct holdings that are microscopic in themselves and through indirect chains; the corporate structure shows the largest registered shareholder at **26.0%**, with the public holding **30.0%** below the disclosure threshold [S11]. Control is therefore not proportionate to economic ownership in any simple sense, which is the classic condition in which holding-company discounts persist rather than close.

Related-party dealings are structural rather than incidental. The group holds short-term investments in PT Bakrie Sumatera Plantations, PT Darma Henwa, PT Bakrie Telecom, PT Bakrieland Development and PT Energi Mega Persada, each of which it describes as an affiliate under common control of the same shareholders and boards, and the audited statements note that related-party terms may differ from those available with third parties [S12]. That disclosure is exactly what a minority holder should weigh when the residual value of the group is negative and the operating companies are small. On pledged shares and board composition, the audited statements and the annual report in the record do not quantify pledges, and we report that as not established rather than as a clean bill [S11, S12].

**Dividend-upstream coverage and look-through leverage.** The method card requires the upstream test, and the answer is stark: no dividend has been received by BNBR from its subsidiaries and none has been paid to shareholders - the payout is nil and the last decision on record was to carry profit to retained earnings [S6]. Upstream coverage of the holdco's own dividend is therefore not a ratio but a nil: there is no upstream cash against which to cover a holdco dividend, because there is no holdco dividend at all, and the group has just raised equity rather than returned it [S5, S6]. Look-through, the debt sits in the parts, not at the parent: the CCT syndicated project loan of **9,715** is at the toll-road subsidiary, the BTI facility of **4,362** owed to Hartman International and Bank Nobu was at the intermediate holding level and has been repaid, and the remainder of the group's **16,748** gross debt sits across the operating subsidiaries [S12, F15, F42]. Against **15,191** of net debt, the parent's claim on the parts is levered by debt it does not control: the toll road's lenders hold the share pledge and set the covenants, so look-through leverage is worse than the headline because the cash flow that services the project loan is trapped at the project [S12, F61].

| Look-through debt, FY2025 | IDR bn | Sits at | Source | |---|---|---|---| | CCT syndicated project loan | 9,715 | toll-road subsidiary | [S12, F15] | | BTI facility (Hartman and Bank Nobu) | 4,362 | intermediate holdco, repaid July 2026 | [S19, F42] | | Group gross debt | 16,748 | consolidated | [S0] | | Group net debt | 15,191 | consolidated | [S0] |

The equity history is the governance issue with teeth. The audited statements show a sequence of capital increases through non-preemptive rights and conversions, and a quasi-reorganization in 2024 that eliminated **19,530** of accumulated deficit, resetting the equity and loss history so that the company's own comparability across years is gone [S11, S12]. The July 2026 rights issue continued the pattern [S16]. On ESG, the integrated annual report carries the group's sustainability framework; nothing in the record suggests an ESG exposure that changes the valuation, and we do not pad the section to imply otherwise. [S11]

**The konglo profile.** BNBR is the Bakrie family's listed holding vehicle, and the house konglo registry records the group and controller directly [S11, S16]. The registry's free-float field is **28.8%**, already above the minimum the exchange now requires; the annual report's separate public-holding figure of **30.0%** is the share held below five per cent each at 31 December 2025, and the small gap between the two is the difference in definition and date, not a discrepancy in ownership [S0, S11]. The registry records BNBR as **not** on the exchange's high-shareholding-concentration list as of 22 October 2026, so the HSC index exclusions do not apply to this name; there is no enforcement action and no index deletion recorded against it. Pledged controller shares are not quantified in the record and we report that as not established [S11, S12]. The related-party balance sheet and the serial equity issuance are the governance features the discount guards against; the float math and the group's capital-markets agenda are what set the marginal price.

The dated catalysts are in the frontmatter: the third-quarter report, which will be the first balance sheet to carry the rights issue and the debt repayment and therefore the first clean read on the group's leverage; the 2026 toll tariff adjustment on the motorway section; the full-year 2026 results, which will show whether the group covers its interest before exceptional items; and the annual meeting, where the accumulated-loss position and any dividend decision sit [S7, S15, S6]. We also watch the interest rate charged on the syndicated facility at each amendment, the traffic and revenue per day the company reports for the toll road against its own budget, whether VKTR becomes covered so the mark can switch from book to house value, and whether the data-centre intention the company has aired becomes a filed, dated and funded project rather than a story [S2, S12].

The KPIs we monitor between updates are the traffic and daily revenue of the toll road, the group's interest cover, net debt as a multiple of EBITDA, the parent-attributable residual after the non-controlling interest, and the share count, which is the number a minority holder should watch most closely in this name [S0, S12].

The holdings marks are unchanged - the live methods carry fixed parts - so the bear moves the discount and the earnings path, not the CCT or VKTR marks; the further-issuance dilution is stated as a risk in the report rather than shocked, because the SOTP is struck on the market share count and a share-count shock would not reach it.

bull.narrative: The discount narrows toward the middle of the band; the scheduled 2026 tariff adjustment and the Burangkeng interchange lift toll traffic faster than plan, so revenue growth is higher; and the cost of debt falls as the post-rights structure and the debt repayment settle. konglo.construction: target = fundamental 12-month value (probability-weighted business scenarios, after the liquidity discount) x the probability-weighted share of today's premium kept, (price / fundamental value today)^(1 - c) over the regime scenarios; c = share of the log gap that closes within 12 months

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E carries the full-year consolidation of the CCT toll road, which entered the group only on 28 November 2025: first-half 2026 revenue of 2,590 (F24) already matches two-thirds of the whole of FY2025, and the company attributes the step to the toll road plus electric-vehicle sales [S15, S5]. Because that is a scope change and not a growth trend, the series steps down to a single-digit rate from FY2027E and holds at the house terminal rate thereafter: FY2027E is set at 8%, sourced to the scheduled 2026 CCT tariff adjustment and to traffic already running above the company's own budget (43,911 vehicles a day, F18), not to a forecast-year spike. [S5, S12, S15, F18]

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Held at the reported first half of 2026 (25.1% of revenue) and not at FY2025's 19.9%, because FY2025 held only one month of a toll road whose gross margin is far above the manufacturing average; the toll road alone ran at 846 revenue and 694 EBITDA in FY2025 on a standalone basis (F33, F34), so weighting the parts lifts the blended margin, and a haircut to the reported ratio would be an unexplained caution [S12, S22]. The ratio is derived from the data pack's first-half quarterly gross-profit lines (374.721 + 275.258 on revenue of 2,592.031 = 25.1%), cited to S0. Those top-line quarterly lines are used because they reconcile to the half-year revenue the company itself reports [S3]; it is the pack's D&A, EBIT and share-count fields that the filing contradicts, not the revenue and gross-profit lines [S0, S3]. Held flat after FY2026E: no disclosed contract or tariff schedule justifies a further step.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Held at the reported first-half 2026 ratio (about 14.2% of revenue) rather than FY2025's 16.8%, which was struck on a revenue base less than half the size of the one the toll road now brings, and because the first-half 2026 income statement already carries the operating expenses of that mix. The 14.2% is derived from the data pack's first-half quarterly operating expense lines (136.787 + 231.142 on revenue of 2,592.031), cited to S0; those lines reconcile to the revenue the company reports, while the pack's EBIT allocation is the field the filing contradicts [S0, S3]. The 16.8% is the audited ratio: Total Beban Usaha of 627.521 on revenue of 3,742.973 (F54, F52, S12). No cost programme is disclosed that would take it lower.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Restated from the audited notes: depreciation and amortisation of 171.363 for FY2025 (F6) against the data pack's 22.921, which is the general-and-administrative allocation only; the charge now also carries the toll road's concession amortisation, so the ratio is set above the FY2025 audited ratio of 4.6%. [S12, F6]

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Held at the reported first-half 2026 run-rate: capex of about 182 in the half against revenue of 2,590, with the toll rest area, the EV assembly facility and the steel businesses still consuming capital; no archived source discloses a taper. [S15, S5]

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Held at the FY2025 ratio (operating working capital of 1,453.9 on revenue of 3,743.0), which is the last audited figure for a group whose receivables are heavily related-party. [S0]

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Set above the FY2025 reported rate of 3.1%, which is distorted by non-taxable bargain-purchase and restructuring gains, and at the low end of the Indonesian corporate range because the group carries tax losses forward after the quasi-reorganization. [S12, S11]

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: The audited FY2025 statements disclose long-term loans at annual rates of 3%-10% (Rupiah) and 1%-7% (US dollar), with the toll road's 9,715.210 syndicated facility (F15) the largest single line and the 2.5% post-rights BTI facility the newest, so the blended cost sits in the middle of that band [S12, S19, F15]. That is consistent with the first half of 2026, the first period to carry the toll road's debt for a full six months: the company posted a net loss of 217 against an operating profit of 301.53 (F43, S3), which leaves room for a net financing cost of roughly five hundred in the half, an effective rate near 6.5% on opening debt of 16,748. This is the first-half rate annualised; it is not the FY2025 ratio, which was struck on a debt balance a fraction of the current one. [S12, S3, F43]

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Set below the disclosed time-deposit rates of 5.0%-6.25% (and 6.75% at end-2025, F48) to allow for the working balances the group keeps outside term deposits, rather than fitted to the first-half interest income. [S12, F48]

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: The rights issue itself is carried in the valuation bridge, not here: the engine's corporate cash-flow template has no line for an equity issuance, so the July 2026 capital action cannot be shown raising cash and repaying debt without driving the modelled cash balance negative - the debt and P&L lines this forecast touches are therefore stated on the pre-issue basis and the repayment is carried in the bridge [S5, S16]. What this line does carry is the funding the continuing business needs: a group that consumes operating cash, pays no dividend and has no equity instrument left funds its deficit and rolling maturities with debt, so the base case assumes it refinances, which is why the modelled cash balance stays non-negative rather than going to minus five thousand as an unfunded forecast would. No specific new facility is disclosed beyond the rest-area borrowing already inside capex, so this is a stated financing assumption at the last actual's scale, not a dated plan. [S5, S12, S19]

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Held at zero in every forecast year. FY2025's other income of 401.969 is dominated by the 320.127 one-off gain on the CCT bargain purchase (F14) plus foreign-exchange and asset-sale gains, and the company's own statement that the first half of 2026 ran at a loss because of the toll road's floating-rate interest says the repeatable line is not there. No archived source forecasts a further one-off. [S12, F14, S5]

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Set at 2% against the audited FY2025 ratio of 1.77%, reflecting the large non-controlling interest the consolidation carries (818.494 at 31 December 2025, of which 812.291 is VKTR, F45) and the fact that minorities absorb their share of the group's losses. [S12, F45]

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Zero. The company has paid no cash dividend in the period covered by the price history and its stated policy makes any payout conditional on financial condition, positive retained earnings and a shareholders' resolution; the last decision on record was to carry profit to retained earnings, and the group has just raised equity rather than returned it. [S6, S5]

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: FY2026E carries the July 2026 rights issue at its filed terms: 14 new Series E shares for every 27 old, which is 0.5185185185 of the count in issue at the last filed balance sheet (F8, F9) [S16, S5]. The ratio is the exact filed one and reconciles the forecast share vector to the pro-forma total of 263,336.672m in F8; nothing is assumed after that.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: House terminal growth for an Indonesian rupiah reporter: long-run nominal GDP, no company-specific claim. [S0]

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: Set at 38%, at the wide end of the 20-40% band the method card says a family holding company's discount persists in, not at the mid-band 33% the first draft used. The red team's C9 is right that 33% had no name-specific anchor; the anchor now used is the set of flags the card says keep a discount wide, every one of which this name carries: a controlling family whose stakes sit behind British Virgin Islands vehicles (F32), a public float of 29.98% (F31), serial equity issuance that has repeatedly reset the share count and most recently struck a rights issue at Rp53, a quasi-reorganization that eliminated 19,530 of accumulated deficit in 2024 (F30), and a dividend record of nil, so cash does not reach the parent's shareholders. The card's dividend-upstream law says a holdco that neither distributes nor covers its own costs deserves the widest discount in its range, which is what 38% is. The discount is applied and not narrowed: the method card makes the discount the base rate, not the opportunity, and this file has no dated discount-narrowing catalyst (no buyback, tender, asset sale, sub-IPO, simplification or control change is dated in the record), so the discount is not credited with narrowing. The 0.38 is a chosen discount level, not the archetype's probability of narrowing: the 'rate' field in data/base_rates.yaml is that success probability and is not read as the discount itself. BNBR's own five-year discount history cannot be computed here - no house sum-of-the-parts exists before this file - so the band plus the flags is the best available anchor. [S11, F30, F31, F32, S16]

challenges.challenge: VKTR is a Bakrie-group konglo member (coverage/universe/konglo.yaml, groups.BAKRIE members include VKTR) with no house model (no coverage/companies/VKTR.JK), yet it is marked at market: 10.677bn shares x Rp675 theoretical ex-rights = Rp7,206.87bn, 66.7% of the Rp10,797.87bn gross parts and the largest single line. VAL_KONGLO_REGIME section 4 says an uncovered konglo sibling "must not be marked at market (its premium would enter the parent's fundamental value): the Director initiates the sibling first and the parent waits in draft." The same defect was a sign-off return on BRPT (queue note). On the book mark the entry itself computes (Rp262.17bn), the SOTP loses Rp6,944.70bn and the fundamental value falls from Rp44 to roughly Rp27 on the engine's own blend arithmetic.
challenges.answer: VKTR is now carried at method: book, not market. The holding is BNBR's share of VKTR net assets from the latest audited balance sheet: VKTR's non-controlling interest of 812.291 at a 75.60% minority implies net assets, of which the 24.40% parent interest is 262.17 (F58), replacing the 7,206.87 market mark. The listed premium (10.677bn shares at the Rp675 theoretical ex-rights price) is excluded, per VAL_KONGLO_REGIME section 4 and the Director's ruling of 28 October 2026 that the stage machine cannot return BNBR to draft. A below-market sensitivity at VKTR's own Rp200 rights-issue price gives 2,135.37 (F57), disclosed in §4 as the sourced floor. The report states plainly that VKTR is uncovered, that its market premium is excluded by the group-consistency rule, and that the mark switches to house value once VKTR publishes. The SOTP, the lens and the report were re-run on the corrected mark (SOTP 19.77/share; fundamental 12-month value 33.57; target 52.22).

challenges.challenge: Section 6 states "the name sits on the exchange's high-shareholding-concentration list, which excludes it from the IHSG calculation and from the LQ45/IDX30/IDX80, and under MSCI's HSC treatment from the MSCI indexes" [S3, S4, S10]. The registry says the opposite: coverage/universe/konglo.yaml has hsc.listed: false as of 2026-10-22, and the engine packet and konglo lens both read HSC False. None of the cited sources (a detik 6M26 results article, a detik FY2025 profit article, a company presentation) contains an HSC list. The report's own section 6 konglo table renders "False", so the prose contradicts its table and the lens has no HSC flag.
challenges.answer: The HSC sentence is deleted and replaced with the registry's own reading: the house konglo registry (as of 22 October 2026) records hsc.listed: false, so the HSC index exclusions do not apply to BNBR, and the report says so in §5 and §6 and in the frontmatter regime catalyst. The contradicted [S3, S4, S10] citations are removed; group and controller come from the annual report. The konglo table already rendered False; the prose now agrees with it. The registry is not believed stale, so no error is flagged to the Director.

challenges.challenge: The P/BV leg mixes bases. Its metric is 3,710.09 (engine market block, latest balance sheet 2026-06-30, before the end-July rights issue) and it divides by 263,336.672m shares (post-rights): 1.963795 x 3,710.09 / 263.337 = Rp27.67. The SOTP adds the Rp4,760bn rights proceeds to NAV through the bridge, but the P/BV leg never adds them to book equity. On post-rights book equity (3,710.09 + 4,760 = 8,470.09) the leg is 8,470.09 x 1.963795 / 263.337 = about Rp63.2, not Rp27.7; the 0.8/0.2 blend then rises from 36.76 to about 43.9 today (fundamental near Rp52, not Rp44). This is the date mismatch the previous review raised as C3, fixed for the SOTP but not for the P/BV leg.
challenges.answer: The P/BV leg is now struck on post-rights book equity. A bs_equity fact (F59) overrides the engine's market-equity field with 8,470.09, being the 30 June 2026 parent equity of 3,710.09 plus the Rp4,760bn July rights proceeds, so the leg divides post-rights equity by the post-rights share count of 263.34bn. The leg moves from 27.67 to 63.16 per share. The blend is re-run (SOTP 19.77 at 0.8, P/BV 63.16 at 0.2) and the §4 "below the primary" divergence paragraph now explains the upward divergence rather than a downward one: book equity is a loose upper reference on the whole consolidated group, not a mark on the parts.

challenges.challenge: The rating is driven by one input. The model's live methods are SOTP (fixed holdings values) and P/BV (fixed market equity); neither consumes revenue growth or cost of debt. The scenario v0 values are exactly the holdco-discount-only results: bear 32.0981 = 0.8 x 58.2557 x (1 - 0.43) + 0.2 x 27.667, and bull 41.4190 = 0.8 x 58.2557 x (1 - 0.23) + 0.2 x 27.667. The +/-3pp revenue-growth and +/-1.5pp cost-of-debt shocks in both scenarios move nothing, while the narratives describe EV profits, manufacturing marks, dilution and cost of debt that the model never applies.
challenges.answer: The report now states plainly that the spread is a discount-only sensitivity: the live methods are the SOTP with fixed part values and the P/BV leg with fixed book equity, so only the holdco-discount shock reaches the blend and the revenue-growth and cost-of-debt shocks move the earnings path and the lens input, not the target. The probabilities are re-weighted from 25/50/25 to bear 35 / base 45 / bull 20 on regime evidence (MSCI froze Indonesian index increases, the HSC list is being removed from the IHSG, OJK has fined the parties behind other konglo cases, and the IHSG fell sharply in the year to October). The bear and bull narratives are rewritten to describe only what the shocks do.

challenges.challenge: The report names the missing bull - "A house-card valuation of that motorway rather than its acquisition mark is what the bull is buying" - but the bull scenario does not re-mark CCT: its shocks are holdco discount, revenue growth and cost of debt only, and CCT is a fixed Rp4,101.321bn (F44), 38.0% of gross parts. The file holds the inputs for a cash-flow check: 43,911 vehicles/day (F18), Rp2.5bn/day revenue (F19) and FY2025 EBITDA of Rp694bn (F33) against revenue of Rp846bn (F34). A re-mark both ways is the largest untested lever after VKTR.
challenges.answer: No sourced CCT house value is computable from the archive. The record carries traffic (43,911 vehicles a day, F18), daily revenue, standalone revenue of 846 and EBITDA of 694 (F33, F34) and the 45-year term to August 2061 (F17), but it contains no tariff schedule and no traffic forecast, so a DCF would have to invent both the tariff path and the growth rate; no disclosed EV/EBITDA for CCT exists in any registered source. An invented path is not a sourced mark, so CCT stays at the audited acquisition fair value (F44), which is the one third-party mark in the file. The upside the red team calls the bull is shown in the new mark sensitivity in §4 and in the bull narrative, and stated as the reason the base is the conservative end of the sourced range. The 45-year term is included (to August 2061); no extension is claimed, and the earlier unsourced extension claim is deleted (C14). The mark moves to a house DCF when a tariff schedule or management traffic forecast is filed.

challenges.challenge: Everything outside CCT and VKTR is a single negative plug of Rp-510.32bn, although those businesses generated FY2025 revenue of Rp2,200bn (BMI, F20), Rp1,080bn (VKTR, F21), Rp464bn (BIIN, F22) and Rp359bn (MKN, F23). A zero floor instead of the negative residual adds Rp510.32bn, about Rp1.2/share after the 33% discount, the 0.8 weight and the 19.6% roll-forward - small, but in the opposite direction to the report's stated bull that they are worth more than book. The line is an accounting plug, not a house valuation, and the prior review's C1 is only partly answered.
challenges.answer: The negative residual is now reconciled in the assumptions basis and in §4 as an arithmetic residual with three sourced causes, not a claim that the businesses are worth zero: the CCT acquisition recognised net assets above the consideration paid, the retained-earnings base is thin after the quasi-reorganization (F30), and the group debt and negative-equity subsidiaries sit here - the Hartman facility (F16) repaid from the rights issue, and Bakrie Metal Industries, whose own non-controlling interest is negative at -1.269 (F60). The zero-floor and a modest positive house mark are stated in the new §4 mark sensitivity and the value is not capitalised because no BMI segment EBITDA or EBIT is archived. The residual is held at book rather than zero so the base is not stacked with caution.

challenges.challenge: The bear narrative says "the manufacturing and EV businesses are marked at zero rather than at book, and the listed VKTR stake is marked down", but no bear shock implements either: the bear shocks are holdco_discount +0.10, revenue_growth -0.03 and cost_of_debt +0.015, and the holdings values are static. Marking the other businesses at zero is bullish against the base (0 versus -510.32, about +Rp1.2/share), and VKTR is not marked down at all. The bear therefore contains the opposite of what it says.
challenges.answer: The bear narrative is rewritten to match the shocks. It no longer says the other businesses are marked at zero or that VKTR is marked down; the part values are fixed, and the bear moves the holdco discount, revenue growth and cost of debt only. The VKTR mark is book in every scenario, so the bear cannot be bullish against it. The bear value is shown by the scenario table and the §5 discount-only statement.

challenges.challenge: The report calls serial equity issuance the governance issue "with teeth" and says the family "dilutes its minority holders a little every cycle", but the bear has no issuance or dilution shock (share_change is static at zero after FY2026E). The leverage risk is never quantified: model net debt/EBITDA is 16,206.57 / 821.28 = 19.7x in FY2026E and interest cover is 563.02 / 1,088.64 = 0.52x, yet the report only says interest is not covered.
challenges.answer: Leverage and cover are now quoted through the forecast: net debt of 16,206.57 and a net-debt/EBITDA of 19.7x in FY2026E, against operating profit of 563.02 and interest of 1,088.64, i.e. cover below one times, using fin. placeholders. Refinancing is explained as a stated, undated model assumption (net new borrowing at the last actual's scale) plus the one dated debt reduction in the record, the July 2026 rights-issue repayment of the BTI facility. Covenant headroom is sourced: the CCT syndicated facility requires positive equity, a debt-to-equity ratio no higher than 6.25x (F61) and a DSCR of at least 100%; the project loan of 9,715.21 is a little over twice the toll road's net asset value of 4,101.32, so DER has headroom and DSCR is the binding, undisclosed test. A further placement is stated as a risk with its probability but not shocked: the SOTP per-share is struck on the market share count, so a share-count shock would not reach it, and a bear-only shock would breach the scenario-mirror gate.

challenges.challenge: The 33% discount is taken mid-band with no name-specific five-year anchor (the file concedes none exists) and no dated narrowing catalyst - section 5 says "we cannot date one". VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT sections 2-3 make the discount the base rate and say "No dated catalyst -> route the idea to EVENT_SPECIAL_SIT standards or pass." Yet the HOLD target of Rp56 is 1.27x the Rp43.97 fundamental value because the konglo lens keeps 30% of a 1.39x premium; the positive 9.4% expected return exists only if that premium survives a regime the report describes as hostile to such names.
challenges.answer: The 33% mid-band discount is replaced with 38%, the wide end of the 20-40% band the method card specifies, anchored to the flags this name carries - offshore control (F32), a public float of 29.98% (F31), serial equity issuance, a quasi-reorganization that erased 19,530 of deficit (F30) and a nil dividend record. The card's dividend-upstream law says a holdco that neither distributes nor covers its own costs deserves the widest discount in its range. The report states plainly that no dated discount-narrowing catalyst exists, so the discount is not credited with narrowing, and it separates the small positive expected return from discount narrowing: that return is the konglo lens's regime carry, which is why the call is HOLD and not ADD. We do not set the target at fundamental value because the konglo card makes the lens the most-likely twelve-month price for a konglo name; the reverse-DCF discussion in §4 is recast accordingly.

challenges.challenge: The frontmatter summary ends "We initiate at Reduce" and calls this an initiation, but the packet rating is HOLD and report_type is update; the body says HOLD. The sign-off summary still carries the v1 rating, so a reader of the summary gets the opposite call to the model.
challenges.answer: The summary is rewritten to the current HOLD/update call, "We initiate at Reduce" is removed, and the frontmatter is checked for v1 residue: version bumped to 3, report_type stays update, the title is refreshed, and the stale regime catalysts that cited company sources for regime facts are replaced. The body already said HOLD; the summary now agrees with the model.

challenges.challenge: VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT's output contract requires a dividend-upstream coverage ratio (sub dividends received versus holdco costs and debt service) and look-through leverage. The report says there is no dividend and that the discount "has nothing to pull against it", but gives no upstream figure and no look-through debt split (CCT project debt versus VKTR versus parent). The consolidated net debt of Rp15,536.0bn / net debt/EBITDA of 19.7x is not decomposed.
challenges.answer: §6 now carries the upstream-coverage statement (nil upstreamed, no holdco dividend to cover, payout nil) and a look-through debt table with sources. The CCT syndicated project loan of 9,715.21 (F15) sits at the toll-road subsidiary; the BTI facility of 4,362.42 (F42) owed to Hartman International and Bank Nobu sat at the intermediate holding level and was repaid from the July 2026 rights issue; the remainder of group gross debt sits across the operating subsidiaries. Group gross and net debt come from the model placeholders.
